builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent
summary: Replaces ad-hoc prompt tuning and leaderboard-score trust with repeated-run stability measurement, trace-based fault attribution by owning layer, and a gated optimization loop that keeps changes only if they beat a pre-registered threshold. Costs include running multiple evaluation passes to quantify variance, maintaining a frozen failure taxonomy, and blind human or multi-model trace review for diagnosis validation. Can fail if run-to-run variance is underestimated on small question sets, leading to false confidence in gains that fall within noise, as the paper itself demonstrates with its accuracy objective.
rationale: The methodology requires only API access to existing models and a fixed evaluation budget, directly addressing the reliability and cost-control problems the reader faces when shipping third-party agents.
technique: Auditable evaluation and intervention loop for agents

claims.statement: Replaces ad-hoc prompt tuning and leaderboard-score trust with repeated-run stability measurement, trace-based fault attribution by owning layer, and a gated optimization loop that keeps changes only if they beat a pre-registered threshold. Costs include running multiple evaluation passes to quantify variance, maintaining a frozen failure taxonomy, and blind human or multi-model trace review for diagnosis validation. Can fail if run-to-run variance is underestimated on small question sets, leading to false confidence in gains that fall within noise, as the paper itself demonstrates with its accuracy objective.

Cost-optimized configuration costs 0.34x the baseline (95% CI [0.22, 0.58]) at accuracy within noise; accuracy objective gains 14 points on dev but only 1.5 on held-out (CI [-5.3, +7.2]), which is within measured run-to-run noise.
